sources.title: Office of the Attorney General; Consolidation of the Office of the Executive Secretariat Into the Justice Management Division

status_summary: A final rule published and effective 2025-12-29 (90 FR 60570, AG Order 6570-2025) removed the Office of the Executive Secretariat as a separate DOJ component and restored its document-clearance functions to a staff within the Justice Management Division, citing deregulatory and streamlining initiatives. This consolidates one management support function; the rule does not mention the Office of Public Affairs or the Office of Legislative Affairs. The department's organization chart page, last modified 2026-06-30, still lists the two offices as separate entries.

timeline.event: DOJ final rule removes the Office of the Executive Secretariat as a separate component and places its functions in the Justice Management Division (28 CFR part 0 amendments).

title: Merge DOJ public and legislative affairs offices and consolidate support functions
uncertainties: The Federal Register rule (90 FR 60570) and the justice.gov organization chart were both read in full and rechecked on 2026-10-18. Federal Register API queries of Department of Justice documents (organization rules since 2025-01-20, and the term consolidation since 2026-01-01, first 20 of 46 results) found no rule concerning public or legislative affairs; internal orders not published in the Federal Register would not appear in that check. A December 2025 Tax Division transfer rule and an August 2026 National Fraud Enforcement Division rule concern litigating functions, not the support functions named in the text. The organization chart does not state reporting lines, so the placement of division public information officers was not verified. The statutory point that the Assistant Attorney General for Legislative Affairs is Senate-confirmed was not checked. congress.gov was not consulted.
